sections.title: Telecom Operating Drivers
sections.subtitle: Quarterly only -- these are not reported as FY totals

charts.title: Data Usage per Customer (GB/month)
charts.annotation: Disclosed in MB through Q4 FY2023 and in GB from Q1 FY2024; this chart shows only the GB-denominated series, so the line starts partway through the history rather than mixing units.

homes.title: Homes (fixed wireless broadband)
homes.content:
Homes customers is the subscriber base for Airtel's fixed-wireless and fibre broadband service; Homes ARPU is average monthly revenue per customer.

For Bharti Airtel: Homes is the fastest-growing of the three fixed-line-adjacent businesses (customers have roughly quadrupled since FY2021) as Airtel pushes fixed-wireless access into homes that never had fixed broadband; ARPU has been declining as the base scales into lower-income cohorts and bundled pricing.

What to watch:

  • Customer growth continuing to outrun mobile growth
  • ARPU trend -- declining ARPU with rising customers is a deliberate land-grab, not necessarily a problem

dth.title: DTH (satellite TV)
dth.content:
DTH customers is the direct-to-home satellite television subscriber base; DTH ARPU is average monthly revenue per customer.

For Bharti Airtel: DTH is the legacy, structurally declining piece of the home-services trio -- the customer base has shrunk since FY2021 as streaming and Homes broadband substitute for satellite TV, even as ARPU has held up through price increases.

What to watch:

  • Whether ARPU gains keep outpacing subscriber attrition on revenue
  • DTH's shrinking share of the combined Homes+DTH customer base

subscriberMix.title: Postpaid and 4G/5G subscriber mix
subscriberMix.content:
4G/5G subscribers and postpaid subscribers are cuts of the total mobile base shown alongside it: 4G/5G is the smartphone/data cohort that drives ARPU, and postpaid is the higher-value, lower-churn plan type.

For Bharti Airtel: the India mobile story is upgrading the base (2G/3G feature-phone users migrating to 4G/5G smartphones) and up-mixing it (prepaid to postpaid) rather than just adding subscribers -- both raise blended ARPU without needing net subscriber growth.

What to watch:

  • 4G/5G and postpaid share of total subscribers rising over time
  • Whether ARPU gains are coming from mix shift or from tariff increases

dataUsage.title: Data usage per customer
dataUsage.content:
Data usage per customer is average monthly data consumption per subscriber, in GB.

For Bharti Airtel: rising per-customer data usage (video and smartphone penetration) is the demand side of the ARPU story -- it is also disclosed in MB through Q4 FY2023 before the company switched to GB reporting from Q1 FY2024; the two series are not shown together to avoid mixing units, so this chart's history starts at the GB switch.

What to watch:

  • Usage growth decelerating as the base saturates
  • Usage growth without matching ARPU growth (data monetisation lag)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Bharti Airtel Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Bharti Airtel Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
